newsitem.title: CHILE: Chilean shares end firm, Andina climbs.
newsitem.headline: Chilean shares end firm, Andina climbs.

text.p: Chilean stocks closed broadly higher in thin trade with gainers including bottler Andina which rallied following the company's share split Monday, dealers said.
The bolsa is seen resuming the rally at the opening, although much will depend on interest in New York for Chilean stocks, they said.
The 40-share index ended up 0.49 percent at 116.65 points. The general index gained 0.24 percent to 5,351.23 points amid volume of nearly 10 billion pesos.
Traders noted the bull run could falter this week if investors decide to cash in gains from the rally which started last week on speculation of lower interest rates.
Andina, Chile's largest soft drinks bottler, climbed as investors reacted positively to the division of its shares into A and B series stocks.
"The creation of the two series was well received by the market, as much for the greater liquidity of the stocks and as experience has shown prices rise after this type of split," said one dealer.
Andina A and B shares both rose 2.36 percent to 1,300 pesos.
Other winners include telecom Entel, up 1.52 percent at 3,015 pesos and steel-maker Cap which rose 1.49 percent to 1,025 pesos.
Decliners included forestry firm Masisa, down 1.75 percent at 225 pesos and copper products manufacturer Madeco which shed 0.89 percent to 1,110 pesos.
